text: 📸 Vivienda para el Bienestar — Reynosa, Tamaulipas (14 ago 2026)

🤝 "You may only look down on someone to help them up." "Pope Francis said it: it is not right to look down at anyone from above; there is only one time you may do it — when you reach out your hand to lift them up. That is 'for the good of all, the poor first.' We give each other a hand, we walk together." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Matamoros Sheinbaum returned to Matamoros, where the program's first stone was laid, to hand over the first homes.
banner: "ONLY LOOK DOWN TO HELP SOMEONE UP"

text: 🏠 "For the good of all, the poor first." "Housing was treated as merchandise and people were told: the poor are poor because they don't work. False. If anyone works, it is the poor — from sunup to sundown. The problem was an economic model that paid hunger wages. We believe in the distribution of wealth." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Matamoros The Vivienda para el Bienestar program targets 1.8M homes; this Matamoros complex was built in 4 months. Families without Infonavit or FOVISSSTE get 0% interest credits.
banner: "FOR THE GOOD OF ALL, THE POOR FIRST"

text: 🏥 1943–1982: 27,000 IMSS hospital beds built. 1982–2018: just 4,000. "In 39 years they built hospitals with 27,000 beds. In the next 36 years, 4,000. Meanwhile the population kept growing, the number of workers kept growing — and chronic diseases arrived: diabetes, hypertension." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Matamoros Two hospitals — ISSSTE Tampico and IMSS Bienestar Ciudad Madero — open this weekend in Tamaulipas. The 12-year goal: 12,000 new beds.

🏘️ Infonavit: from 140bn to 1.13tn pesos — and no more loan requirements. "We found 4,856,000 credits that grew even as people paid. The Infonavit had become the worst bank in the world — a loan-sharking, thieving bank. The President gave us one instruction: solve it in favor of the people." — Octavio Romero, Infonavit director, Reynosa All unpayable credits were restructured by Dec 31. Gone are the 30 requirements and 1,080 points: a loan now needs only 3 conditions — be a member, have 6 months on the job, earn 1–2.9 minimum wages.

💪 Minimum wage up 3.4× — no inflation, record investment, strongest peso ever. "They said: if the minimum wage goes up there will be inflation, there will be no investment, the peso will be devalued. Well, it went from 2,800 pesos a month in 2018 to more than 9,500. And there is no inflation, foreign direct investment is at a record, and the peso is stronger than ever — one of the strongest currencies in the world." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Reynosa Sheinbaum spoke at a Vivienda para el Bienestar handover in Reynosa, Tamaulipas, part of a weekend tour of the state.

🏠 "It's called corruption and robbery... This is called justice." "A woman borrowed 63,000 pesos, paid 380,000, and still owed 2 million. How is that possible? It's called corruption and robbery — there is no other name for it. And what do these families owe now? Zero. Some say: how can you forgive those credits? This is called justice, social justice for the working people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Reynosa Nearly 4.9M families held Infonavit mortgages that kept growing as they paid. All were restructured or forgiven; 288,000 of them in Tamaulipas alone.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO'S HEAVY-TRUCK INDUSTRY ROARS BACK: OUTPUT +51.8%, EXPORTS +66.7%</u>

Mexican plants built 14,675 trucks, buses and tractor-trailers in July — 51.8% more than a year ago — and exported 13,117 units, up 66.7%, industry group ANPACT reported (El Economista).

The industry is pressing Washington to adjust Section 232 tariffs and fighting a flood of used American trucks: for every 100 new units sold in Mexico, about 53 used ones cross the border. ANPACT says it is working with Mexico's Treasury to stop customs undervaluation.

Its message to T-MEC negotiators: "preserve the principles that have made the treaty successful — clear rules and certainty that favor investment, the integration of supply chains, well-paid jobs and regional competitiveness."

🇲🇽✊ <u>TLAXCALA'S INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES CO-WRITE MEXICO'S NEW RIGHTS LAW</u>

Representatives of 70 Nahua and Otomí communities across 19 municipalities joined the national consultation for Mexico's new General Law on the Rights of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Peoples — one of 82 regional assemblies feeding the bill President Sheinbaum will send to Congress on October 12.

"Mexico cannot be built without the voice of its original peoples," said Governor Lorena Cuéllar.

The same day, the INPI opened a coordination center in Tlaxcala's Palacio de Cultura — a direct answer to a request community authorities made to the President herself, so the institute's territorial structure sits at the service of the peoples it exists for.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>'THE PRIAN DEFENDS LIES': MORENA FIRES BACK AFTER INE CRACKDOWN ON 'NARCOPARTY' SMEARS</u>

Mexico's electoral authority ordered the PRI and PAN to stop spreading fabricated claims tying Morena to drug trafficking — and the opposition suddenly discovered "censorship."

"It's increasingly clear that the opposition, the PRIAN, what they defend are lies," said Morena president Ariadna Montiel. She recalled the 2006 "a danger to Mexico" campaign against AMLO: he would take your house, turn Mexico into Venezuela. "None of that happened."

Meanwhile, Alito Moreno just made his third Washington trip of the year — February, May, August — lobbying the US to brand Morena a criminal organization while his own impeachment file for illicit enrichment sits in the Chamber of Deputies.
banner: INE ORDERS PRIAN: STOP THE LIES
